neighbours.label: reflexive pronoun (yourself, themselves) as the object of a preposition at the end of a longer advice passage ('stories about yourself', 'time for yourself'); a weak, context-hungry pole whose + side is 'N years [and older]'
fire: Starting at a new school can feel lonely at first. A good way to make friends in your class is to tell them a little about yourself and your family.
A clean kitchen matters more than most people think. Washing your hands before cooking is the simplest way to protect both yourself and your guests.
Long flights are tiring, so plan ahead. Pack a small bag with snacks and a book so that you have something for yourself and your children.
Writing a cover letter does not need to be hard. Use the first paragraph to give the employer some basic facts about yourself and your experience.
Winter storms can knock out power for days. Keep extra blankets and water in the house so that you can take care of yourself and your pets.
Retirement comes sooner than you expect. Saving a little every month is the surest way to build a secure future for yourself and your partner.
New parents often forget to rest. The group teaches young mothers and fathers how to make time for themselves and their friends.
Refugee families arrive with very little. The charity helps them find work so that they can provide for themselves and their children.
